acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Crocodilians family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Snarejaw, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Bank-Drag Specialist archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Long-snouted crocodilian with reinforced jaw hinge, unusual lateral neck flexibility, narrow body, and visible sensory pits.
Signature mechanic: Crescent Snare: the far jaw tip traces a semicircle around cover before the hinge closes and drags sideways.
battlefieldDuty: Sweep an elongated jaw around cover, close behind a target, and drag laterally along the shoreline.
constructionDimensions: Layered wet hide, refractive scute channels, coherent body-edge currents, and controlled pressure sacs preserve solid anatomy.
Wakes, drag lines, channel rises, and draining belly seams explain exactly how water powers each attack.
counterplay: Step toward the head hinge or strike the narrow jaw side before closure. Affinity signal: The pressurized jaw, flank, or tail channel drains after release and exposes the same hinge or belly fault.
forbiddenTreatments: Opaque floodwater that hides the animal or channel order
identityInvariants: Every form retains a low four-legged crocodilian body, long tail, scuted back, belly fault, sensory pits, and a jaw-driven attack silhouette.
Tier escalation uses snout geometry, scute height, neck mobility, tail mass, scars, and waterline behavior rather than equipment or wings.
Eyes, wake direction, jaw angle, foreclaw grooves, tail curve, and exposed belly keep ambush and rotation counterplay readable.
telegraph: The far jaw tip taps the ground and the flexible neck bends into a visible crescent.
